# Ancestorii

> Ancestorii is a family memory platform, made in the UK, with two layers: My Family, a private space where invited relatives keep their photos, videos, voice notes, written memories, timelines and time capsules together, and Our Stories, a free public feed of real family stories that anyone can read. Families can also turn their photos into printed keepsakes: hardcover Memory Books, canvas prints and acrylic prints. It works on the website and in a free iPhone and Android app, with one login for both. The Free plan needs no card, and Premium is £3.99 a month for the whole family.

## What Ancestorii is

Family memories end up scattered across phones, hard drives, shoeboxes, group chats and social media, where they get buried or lose their meaning. Ancestorii gives a family one private place for them: written memories with photos, video and voice notes; a profile for each person who shaped the family; albums, timelines and time capsules; and a shared Library for the photos and videos the family wants to keep and print. Relatives join by invitation and add their own memories, and when two people remember the same moment differently, both versions are kept side by side. Families can publish chosen stories to Our Stories, the free public feed, and order printed keepsakes designed from their own photos. Ancestorii calls this a living library rather than a digital vault: a vault holds files, while a living library keeps the people, stories and voices behind them and grows as the family adds to it. The name blends "ancestors" and "story". The double "i" stands for two people, the one telling the story and the one receiving it, because memory survives in the handoff.

## The two layers

1. **Our Stories (public, free for everyone)**: a public feed of real family stories at https://www.ancestorii.com/stories. Anyone can read it without an account, and story pages can appear in search engines. Members can publish their own stories, give hearts, comment and share, free forever. Our Stories is on the website only.
2. **My Family (private)**: the family's own space. Only people invited into the family space can see it, and nothing in it becomes public unless a member chooses to publish it as a story on Our Stories. It has a Free plan (no card needed) and one paid plan, Premium, at £3.99 a month for the whole family.

## Features

### My Family (private)

- **Private family feed**: write a memory in your own words, with up to 10 photos, one video and a voice note, and it appears in a feed that only your family can see. Relatives give hearts, comment in writing or by voice, and add their own voice notes. The feed is in the iPhone and Android app; single memories also open on the website from notifications and emails.
- **Multiple perspectives**: when relatives remember the same moment differently, each can add their own version to the same memory, shown side by side as tabs.
- **Questions**: send a relative one of 46 ready-made questions in 10 chapters (Growing Up; Holidays & Traditions; Around the Table; Love & Relationships; Life Lessons; The Stories We Retell; Work & Purpose; Adventures & Travel; Only You Would Know; Music & Hobbies), or write your own. They answer in the app, the answer is saved as a memory marked "In response to" your question, and you get an email. Question links are time-limited. Questions are sent and answered in the app only; on a phone without the app, the link opens the App Store or Google Play.
- **Loved Ones**: a private profile for each person who shaped your family, living or passed: photo, relationship, birth and death dates, a life story in four chapters (Early years, Important moments, Special memories, Who they are) and the albums, timelines and capsules they appear in. The Free plan includes 1 Loved One profile; Premium includes unlimited. Website and app.
- **Albums**: group photos and videos, then give each picture a date, a story thread the family adds to, and voice notes. Unlimited on every plan. Website and app.
- **Timelines**: lay out a life in dated events with photos, video, family comments and voice notes, and download the timeline as a PDF on the website. Unlimited on every plan. In the app, and on the website on screens at least 1,024 pixels wide.
- **Capsules (digital time capsules)**: seal photos, videos, a letter and voice notes until a date you choose. Once sealed, a capsule shows as locked with a countdown, and Ancestorii won't let you open or edit it until that date, when it opens for the family automatically. The seal is there to keep a surprise, not to guard a secret. Unlimited on every plan. Website.
- **Library**: one shared library for the photos and videos the family uploads to it, sorted into folders. Photos can be picked from it for albums, capsules, timelines and printed keepsakes, and photos uploaded while designing a print are saved to it too (in Uncategorised). Photos uploaded straight into an album, capsule or timeline stay there and are not copied into the Library. iPhone HEIC photos are converted to JPEG automatically. Website.
- **Voice notes**: record or upload voice notes on album photos, timeline moments, capsules, private memories and Our Stories posts. Every new recording is converted to M4A so it plays on any phone. Website and app.
- **Invite family**: Owners and Admins invite relatives with one reusable share link (to send by WhatsApp or text) or a personal email invite, which expires after 7 days. There is no limit on family members on any plan. The roles are Owner, Admin and Member; everyone in the family space sees everything in it, and only the person who added something can delete it. Inviting happens on the website, and sending a question from the app can invite someone too.
- **Story Assistance (optional writing help)**: AI suggestions, made with Claude by Anthropic, that offer guiding questions, openings, captions and short drafts on Loved Ones, albums, timelines, capsules, Memory Books, memories and Our Stories. You choose what to keep, and it never rewrites your words automatically. It is on by default and can be switched off in your profile settings. Ancestorii's privacy policy says inputs are not used to train AI models. Website.
- **Rewards**: as a family saves memories together, it unlocks rewards: a Verified Family badge at 5 memories, print discounts from 10% up to 50%, and free prints at higher milestones (some need at least two family members contributing). Reward codes are earned in the app, are single-use, last 7 days and are redeemed at print checkout on the website. Delivery is still charged, and a reward code replaces the Premium discount rather than adding to it.
- **Notifications**: in-app notifications and phone push in the app when someone hearts or comments on a memory, adds their side of it or joins the family, plus emails, for example when a relative answers your question, someone joins the family, someone comments on your public story, or a print order is confirmed and shipped.

### Our Stories (public)

- **Reading**: free, with no account needed. Stories are grouped into seven topics: Family, Food & Recipes, Childhood, Love, Life Lessons, Traditions and Travel, each with its own page.
- **Feed order**: newest stories first by default, and everyone sees the same feed: it is not personalised and there are no follower counts. Readers can sort by Most Loved (hearts) or Most Discussed (comments), a Trending Stories box shows the most-loved recent stories, and the Ancestorii team can feature a story.
- **Publishing**: a title, a topic, a short preview and the story itself, with up to 10 photos, one video (up to 5 minutes on Free, 15 on Premium) and a voice note. Optional writing help offers "Help me start", "Help me go deeper" and "Help me end it".
- **Hearts, comments and sharing**: readers give hearts, reply in comment threads and share stories, and the author is notified.
- **Community standards**: only genuine family memories. No religious or political content, hate speech, harassment, discrimination, spam, self-promotion or commercial content. Each story is checked automatically when it is published, using Claude by Anthropic: stories that pass go live straight away, and flagged stories wait for a person to review them. Signed-in readers can report a story. A three-strike policy applies to the public feed only: first, removal and an email explaining why; second, removal, a final warning and a 7-day publishing suspension; third, a permanent ban from Our Stories. Strikes never affect a family's private My Family space.
- **Always your choice**: nothing from My Family goes public unless you publish it, and you can take a published story down at any time.

### Printed keepsakes (Heirlooms)

Memory Books, canvas prints and acrylic prints, designed on the website from the family Library. Sizes, prices and delivery are under "Printed keepsakes: prices and delivery" below.

## Where each feature works

- **iPhone and Android app**: the private family feed (writing and reading memories), questions (sending and answering) and earning rewards, plus albums, timelines, voice notes and Loved Ones profiles.
- **Website**: Our Stories (reading, publishing, hearts and comments), capsules, the Library, inviting family, Story Assistance, upgrading to Premium, designing and ordering printed keepsakes and redeeming reward codes, plus albums, timelines (on screens at least 1,024 pixels wide), voice notes and Loved Ones profiles.
- **One account**: the same email and password work in the app and on the website. The app is free and has no in-app purchases.

## Plans and pricing

### Our Stories: free forever

Reading, hearts, comments, sharing and publishing your own stories are free for everyone. Reading needs no account.

### My Family: Free plan

- £0, with no card needed. It is not a trial and has no end date.
- 1 GB storage allowance, shared by the whole family.
- File size allowance of up to 20 MB per file.
- Videos up to 5 minutes long.
- Unlimited albums, timelines and capsules.
- 1 Loved One profile.
- No limit on family members.

### My Family: Premium plan

- £3.99 a month per family (or €4.99 or $5.99 a month, chosen on the Plans page). One subscription covers everyone in the family space, not just one person.
- 100 GB storage allowance, shared by the whole family.
- File size allowance of up to 10 GB per file.
- Videos up to 15 minutes long.
- Unlimited albums, timelines and capsules.
- Unlimited Loved One profiles.
- No limit on family members.
- Priority support and early access to new features.
- 10% off Memory Books, canvas prints and acrylic prints, applied automatically at checkout.
- Monthly only: there is no annual plan and no free trial. Upgrading happens on the website.

### Cancelling and downgrading

Premium can be cancelled at any time through the Help page form or by emailing support@ancestorii.com. It lasts to the end of the billing period, then the family returns to the Free plan, and partial periods are not refunded. Nothing is deleted: everything stays viewable, and only new uploads beyond the Free allowances pause.

### No ads

Ancestorii shows no ads and does not sell, rent or trade personal data.

## Printed keepsakes: prices and delivery

Printed keepsakes are paid for per order, with no subscription needed. They are designed on the website, then printed and shipped by Prodigi, Ancestorii's print partner. Every price is for one item, plus delivery.

### Memory Books: from £44.99 plus delivery

- An A4 landscape hardcover book (297 × 210 mm) with a matte-finish cover and 200gsm gloss pages, designed page by page.
- Three sizes: A Chapter, 24 pages, £44.99 ($59.99, €49.99); A Story, 36 pages, £54.99 ($74.99, €64.99), the most popular; A Legacy, 48 pages, £64.99 ($84.99, €74.99). The size can't be changed once a book is started.
- Five page layouts (Portrait, Landscape, Duo, Grid, Feature), three front covers (Classic, Full Bleed, Trio), three back covers (Blank, Dedication, Photo + Message) and a spine with your own text and colours. Each photo can have a subheading and a written comment.
- Preview the book spread by spread, and download a free PDF of the design.
- The printed book holds photos and written words. It has no audio or QR codes.
- Each order prints one copy. For more copies, place the order again; delivery is charged on each order.

### Canvas prints: from £99.99 plus delivery

- The Moment, 16 × 36 in, £99.99 ($139.99, €119.99); The Heirloom, 20 × 32 in, £129.99 ($179.99, €154.99), the recommended size; The Heritage, 24 × 72 in, £169.99 ($229.99, €199.99), delivered to UK addresses only.
- 400gsm canvas on a 38mm stretcher bar, with an image wrap finish (the picture carries on around the sides).
- Landscape or portrait, chosen at the start, with 1 to 10 photos in layouts that vary by size and orientation.

### Acrylic prints: from £99.99 plus delivery

- The Portrait, 16 × 24 in, £99.99 ($139.99, €119.99); The Centrepiece, 24 × 24 in, £149.99 ($199.99, €179.99), the recommended size; The Masterpiece, 24 × 36 in, £199.99 ($269.99, €239.99).
- The photo is printed behind a crystal-clear acrylic panel, with float-mount hanging hardware included.
- Three layouts: Solo (1 photo), Duo (2 photos) and Grid (4 photos).

### Delivery, currency and orders

- Delivery is charged on every order. Standard delivery costs £4.99 ($5.99, €5.99) and takes an estimated 10 to 14 working days. Canvas and acrylic prints can also go Express for £8.99 ($10.99, €9.99), an estimated 5 to 7 working days. Delivery times are estimates, not guarantees.
- Prints are delivered to 20 countries: the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands, Belgium, Austria, Switzerland, Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland, Portugal and Poland. The Heritage canvas is delivered to UK addresses only.
- Orders are charged in pounds, euros or US dollars, chosen automatically at checkout.
- Premium families get 10% off automatically. Discounts don't stack: a reward code replaces the Premium discount.
- Printing starts as soon as payment goes through, so orders can't be cancelled after checkout. Prints are made to order and are replaced or refunded only if they arrive damaged, defective or materially different from the order, reported within 14 days of delivery with photos.
- Customers get an order confirmation email, a shipping email with a tracking link, and an Orders page that follows each order.

## Privacy and data

- My Family is private to the members of each family space, and that rule is enforced in the database, not just in the app. Private photos, videos and voice notes are kept in private storage and shown through short-lived signed links.
- Our Stories is public by design: anyone can read published stories and see their photos.
- You keep ownership of everything you upload. Ancestorii holds only the limited licence it needs to run the service, make print files and show what you choose to publish.
- No ads, and personal data is not sold, rented or traded.
- Accounts are for people aged 16 or over, and under-18s need a parent's consent.
- To delete an account, go to Profile, then Delete Account, in the app, or email support@ancestorii.com from the address you registered with.
- The data controller is Ancestorii Ltd, registered with the UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO registration ZC149600).

## The app

- Free on iPhone (https://apps.apple.com/app/id6784750387) and Android (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ancestorii.app).
- In the app: the private family feed, questions, albums, timelines, voice notes, Loved Ones profiles and rewards.
- On the website: Our Stories, capsules, the Library, upgrades and printed keepsake orders.
- No in-app purchases. The same email and password work in the app and on the website.

## Who Ancestorii is for

- Families who don't want their history scattered across phones or lost when someone changes a device.
- Adult children who want to capture their parents' and grandparents' stories, voices and photos while they can.
- Parents and grandparents who want to pass their stories on in their own words.
- Anyone who has been meaning to write things down but never has.
- People who have lost someone and want to keep their memory, voice and stories together.
- Families looking for a meaningful, personal gift: a Memory Book, a canvas print or an acrylic print.

## How Ancestorii compares

- **Cloud photo storage (Google Photos, iCloud, Dropbox)**: built to back up every file. Ancestorii keeps the story, the date and the voices behind the photos that matter, in a private space the family adds to. The two work well side by side.
- **Group chats and social media (WhatsApp, Facebook groups)**: built for conversation, so photos get buried in the scroll, and Facebook is funded by ads. Ancestorii is ad-free and private to the family you invite, and memories stay organised by person, album and timeline.
- **Genealogy sites (Ancestry, MyHeritage)**: built for researching records and building family trees. Ancestorii keeps the family's own photos, voices and stories, and is not a genealogy research service. They work well together.
- **Prompt-and-book services (Storyworth, Remento)**: built around one storyteller answering prompts to make a book. Ancestorii is a private space the whole family adds to over time, and any printed book is one you design yourself, page by page.
- **Baby journals (Tinybeans)**: built to share one child's photos with family. Ancestorii is for every generation's photos, voices and stories.

## Founder

Ancestorii was founded in 2025 by Dante Leon, its sole founder, in the United Kingdom. Dante works full time as an aircraft mechanic for British Airways on a four-days-on, four-days-off rota, and builds Ancestorii on his days off, on his own, on a laptop, with no team or investors. He built it because he was scared of losing the small things: the way his grandmother hummed while she cooked and described the village she grew up in, and the sound of his mum laughing at her own jokes before she reached the punchline. He could not find one place that held the story, the photo and the voice together. His letter about why he built it is at https://www.ancestorii.com/why-this-exists, and Ancestorii's guides are written under his name.

- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/dante-leon-10baaa17a/
- Reddit: https://www.reddit.com/user/keepingmemories/ (u/keepingmemories)

## Technology

Ancestorii is built with Next.js and Supabase. Payments go through Stripe, printed keepsakes are made and shipped by Prodigi, emails are sent with Resend, and Story Assistance and the Our Stories checks use Claude, made by Anthropic.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Ancestorii free?**
Yes, to start. Our Stories is free forever, and My Family has a Free plan with no card needed: a 1 GB family storage allowance, unlimited albums, timelines and capsules, and 1 Loved One profile. Premium costs £3.99 a month for the whole family.

**Is my family space private?**
Yes. Only the people invited into your family space can see My Family. Nothing in it appears on Our Stories, in search results or anywhere public unless you choose to publish it as a story.

**How many family members can join?**
There is no limit on family members on either plan, and Premium covers the whole family under one subscription.

**Do I need the app?**
For some things. The private family feed and questions are in the free iPhone and Android app. Our Stories, capsules, the Library, upgrades and print orders are on the website. Albums, timelines, voice notes and Loved Ones work in both.

**What happens if I stop paying for Premium?**
Nothing is deleted. The family returns to the Free plan at the end of the billing period, everything stays viewable, and only new uploads beyond the Free allowances pause.

**Who owns what I upload?**
You do. Ancestorii holds only the limited licence it needs to run the service.

**Does Ancestorii use AI?**
In two places. Story Assistance is optional writing help that suggests questions, openings and short drafts you can use or ignore, and it can be switched off. Each story published to Our Stories is also checked automatically against the community standards.

**Can I order more than one copy of a Memory Book?**
Yes, by placing the order again. Each order prints one copy, and delivery is charged on each order.

**Does a printed Memory Book include voice recordings?**
No. Printed books hold photos and written words. Voice notes stay in the family's Ancestorii space.

**Where do you deliver printed keepsakes?**
To 20 countries: the UK and Ireland, 14 more countries in Europe, the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. The Heritage canvas is delivered to UK addresses only.

**How is Ancestorii different from Ancestry?**
Ancestry is for researching records and building a family tree. Ancestorii is for keeping your family's own photos, voices and stories. The two work well together.

### Guides: photos and archives

- [What to do with old family photos](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/what-to-do-with-old-family-photos): Turn scattered images into something your family actually wants to return to.
- [How to digitise old photos](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-digitize-old-photos): The scan settings archives use: 300 dpi for most prints, a TIFF master, dated file names and two copies.
- [How to scan photos with your phone](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-scan-photos-with-your-phone): Soft daylight, a glare-free app and the phone held square: good scans without a scanner.
- [How to digitise slides and negatives](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-digitize-slides-and-negatives): Film needs far more resolution than a print. How to scan it, and how to spot vinegar syndrome early.
- [How to digitise old home videos](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-digitize-home-videos): Copy VHS and camcorder tapes yourself, send cine film to a specialist, and keep the right files.
- [How to organise family photos](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-organize-family-photos): Gather every photo in one place, keep the best of each, name files by date and tag the people.
- [How to label old photos, and what to write](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-label-old-photos): Soft pencil on the back edge, never ballpoint or sticky labels, and the who, where and when.
- [How to store old photos so they last](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-store-old-photos): Keep them cool, dry, dark and steady, in the right boxes, and out of lofts and damp cellars.
- [How long do photos last?](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-long-do-photos-last): Prints, slides, discs and drives all age differently: what lasts, what fades and what can fail.
- [How to back up family photos](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-back-up-family-photos): The 3-2-1 rule: three copies, on two kinds of storage, with one kept away from home.
- [How to preserve old letters and documents](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-preserve-old-letters-and-documents): Store them flat in acid-free folders, never laminate or tape them, and scan each page for the family to read.

### Guides: voices and stories

- [How to preserve family memories](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-preserve-family-memories): A starting point for anyone who has been meaning to write things down but never has.
- [How to record family stories](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-record-family-stories): Simple ways to capture the stories that only get told when a certain person is in the room.
- [How to save family voices](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-save-family-voices): Because the way someone tells a story matters as much as the story itself.
- [How to digitise cassette tapes](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-digitize-cassette-tapes): Tape has a limited life. How to record cassettes to WAV at home and keep the files safe.
- [How to get your family to share their memories](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-get-family-to-share-memories): Ask one small question at a time, let them answer from their phone, and welcome different versions of a story.
- [How to write a life story](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-write-a-life-story): Start with a timeline, gather stories in their own words, then shape them into chapters with photos.
- [How to preserve family recipes](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-preserve-family-recipes): Scan the handwritten card, add modern measurements and cook it with the person who made it.
- [What to write in a memory book](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/what-to-write-in-a-memory-book): How to fill the blank page so the finished book is one your family actually returns to.

### Guides: questions to ask

- [Questions to ask your parents about their life](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/questions-to-ask-your-parents-about-their-life): Thirty questions, grouped by theme, for asking while you still can.
- [Questions to ask your mum](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/questions-to-ask-your-mum): Her childhood, her own mother, her work and the years before you, with Mothering Sunday ideas.
- [Questions to ask your dad](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/questions-to-ask-your-dad): His childhood, his own father, his first jobs and the stories he rarely tells, with Father's Day ideas.
- [Questions to ask your grandparents, decade by decade](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/questions-to-ask-your-grandparents): Questions tied to moments they lived through, from rationing to the 1953 Coronation and Decimal Day.
- [How to interview your grandparents](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-interview-your-grandparents): Pick one theme, ask open questions, record with a clip-on mic and agree in writing how it's used.

### Guides: remembrance

- [How to keep memories of a loved one alive](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-keep-memories-of-a-loved-one-alive): Save their voice and messages, write their stories down while they're fresh and keep talking about them.
- [How to save voicemails from a loved one](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-save-voicemails-from-a-loved-one): Networks can erase voicemail. How to keep their messages as audio files, on iPhone, Android and landlines.
- [How to save text messages from a loved one](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-save-text-messages-from-a-loved-one): Stop your phone deleting old chats, then keep your own copies of their texts and WhatsApp messages.
- [How to make a memorial book](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-make-a-memorial-book): Gather photos and memories from the family, put the pages in the order of their life and leave time to print.
- [How to write a eulogy](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-write-a-eulogy): Five to ten minutes and two or three true stories: how to gather them, shape it and get through it.

### Guides: time capsules and legacy

- [What to put in a time capsule](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/what-to-put-in-a-time-capsule): Letters, named photos, today's front page and your voices, plus what to leave out and which container to use.
- [How to write a legacy letter](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-write-a-legacy-letter): Pass on your stories, values and hopes rather than possessions: what to include and where to keep it.
- [What happens to your photos when you die?](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/what-happens-to-your-photos-when-you-die): Without a plan, cloud photos can be locked away or deleted. The legacy settings at Apple, Google and Facebook.

### Guides: gifts and occasions

- [Gifts for grandparents that mean something](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/gifts-for-grandparents): Photo books, framed prints, recorded voices and time together, plus when Grandparents' Day falls.
- [80th birthday ideas that celebrate a whole life](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/80th-birthday-ideas): A memory book of eight decades, letters from the family and a party built around their stories.
- [Wedding anniversary gifts by year](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/anniversary-gift-ideas-by-year): Paper, cotton and leather through to ruby, gold and diamond: the traditional British list, with gift ideas.
- [Family tradition ideas worth starting](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/family-traditions-ideas): Small, repeatable traditions, from the same photo every birthday to a recipe cooked on the same day each year.

### Guides: family history

- [Family history vs family tree: what's the difference?](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/family-history-vs-family-tree): A tree records who connects to whom; family history tells who they were. How the two fit together.
- [How to start researching your family history](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-start-researching-your-family-history): Begin with living relatives, then work back through UK certificates, census returns and the 1939 Register.
- [How to create a family archive](https://www.ancestorii.com/guides/how-to-create-a-family-archive): Decide what to keep, store the originals safely, digitise the best and note who, what, when and why.
